subject: Architecture
title: Passive House: The Ultra-Efficient Standard
description: A quick, practical guide to Passive House: The Ultra-Efficient Standard.

hook.text: Passive House buildings use 90% less energy for heating and cooling than conventional structures.

buildup.text: The standard demands extreme insulation, airtight construction, and heat-recovery ventilation.

discovery.text: A Passive House can be heated by body warmth and appliances alone — no furnace or boiler needed.

twist.text: The concept was invented in Germany in 1991 but originally inspired by a Canadian research project.

climax.text: Over 65,000 Passive House buildings now exist worldwide — from Arctic cabins to tropical apartments.

punchline.text: The house is so well insulated that you are the heater.

quiz.question: How much less energy does a Passive House use for heating and cooling?

details.summary: Passive House buildings use up to 90% less heating and cooling energy than conventional structures. This is achieved through extreme insulation, airtight construction, triple-glazed windows, thermal bridge-free design.
details.whyItMatters: Passive House proves that radical energy reduction is achievable with existing technology and no sacrifice in comfort. By rethinking building envelopes rather than adding complex systems, it offers the simplest path to near-zero-energy buildings.
takeaways: Uses up to 90% less heating and cooling energy than standard buildings
Achieved through insulation, airtightness, and heat recovery ventilation
Requires no special heating or cooling equipment

faq.question: Is a Passive House completely sealed?
faq.answer: The envelope is airtight to prevent uncontrolled heat loss, but mechanical ventilation with heat recovery (MVHR) provides constant fresh air. The MVHR recovers up to 90% of heat from outgoing stale air and transfers it to incoming fresh air, maintaining air quality without energy waste.

faq.question: Does Passive House cost more to build?
faq.answer: Typically 5-15% more in construction costs, depending on climate and building type. However, the dramatically reduced energy bills recoup the premium within 5-10 years. Over the building's lifetime, Passive House construction saves money compared to conventional building with standard codes.
